r.정치 구도: A federal parliamentary system made up of regional states drawn largely along ethnic lines. The 1995 constitution even gives each nation and nationality the right to secede. From 1991 to 2018 a coalition dominated by the Tigray People's Liberation Front from the north ran the country; after a reformist prime minister took office in 2018, the ruling coalition was remade as the Prosperity Party. Pushed aside in the process, the TPLF fought a war with the federal government from 2020 to 2022, and the Pretoria peace agreement of November 2022 ended the large-scale fighting. Since 2023, however, a militia known as Fano has been fighting government forces in the Amhara region, and in October 2026 heavy fighting broke out again in Tigray, with federal forces retaking the regional capital, Mekelle. The Prosperity Party won an overwhelming majority in the June 2026 election, which critics said was held amid serious insecurity.

t.why: With well over 100 million people it is Africa's second most populous country after Nigeria, and the African Union's headquarters in Addis Ababa make it a hub of African diplomacy. It lost its coastline when Eritrea became independent in 1993, so it relies on neighboring Djibouti's port for most of its trade, and the government has made access to the sea a national goal. That has raised tensions with Eritrea, which holds the Red Sea port of Assab, and in 2026 Eritrea cut diplomatic ties with Ethiopia. In September 2025 it completed Africa's largest hydropower dam on the upper Nile, over fierce objections from Egypt and Sudan, which depend on the river for most of their water. It joined BRICS in January 2024, and the same year let its currency float as part of a support program with the IMF.
t.rel: Its desire for access to the sea has raised tension with Eritrea and Somalia. It signed a peace deal with Eritrea in 2018 after their 1998 border war, but relations have soured again. It is at odds with Egypt and Sudan over its huge Nile dam.
t.korea: During the Korean War it sent the Kagnew Battalion, drawn from the emperor's Imperial Bodyguard, in successive rotations from 1951 to 1954. It was the only African country to send ground troops, and 121 of its soldiers were killed. Diplomatic relations were established in December 1963, and Chuncheon is home to a memorial hall for Ethiopia's Korean War veterans. In 2013 Ethiopian Airlines launched direct flights between Addis Ababa and Incheon, still the only direct air link between Africa and Korea. Coffee makes up most of what Korea buys from Ethiopia.
t.know: Ethiopia uses its own 13-month calendar, which runs seven to eight years behind the Western one.
etext: Ethiopian Airlines is widely seen as Africa's largest airline and has made Addis Ababa airport a transfer hub linking Africa with Asia, Europe and the Americas. It is one of the country's biggest earners of foreign currency.
As the birthplace of coffee, its biggest export is coffee, along with flowers and sesame. A large share of the workforce relies on farming.

Rivers rushing down from the highlands give it excellent conditions for hydropower. With its giant dam now complete, it aims to earn foreign currency by selling electricity to neighbors such as Kenya and Djibouti.

Being landlocked makes shipping costly, and a chronic shortage of foreign currency makes it hard for factories to import materials. It missed a bond interest payment at the end of 2023 and entered debt restructuring, and ongoing internal conflict deters investment.
